newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks amble to just firmer close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks amble to just firmer close.

text.p: The Australian share market ambled to a just firmer close on Monday with the market buoyed by a bank sector boosted by hopes of local interest rate cuts and a U.S. bond market rally.
The All Ordinaries index added 3.2 points to 2,426.9.
The benchmark indicator spent the most of the day wandering in an eight point range with little inspiration for traders to commit to either side of the market.
"The interest rate cut is in the back of people's minds," said a senior dealer at a Sydney brokerage, but adding that there were other reasons for investor reluctance.
"News Corp's results are also coming up and with Wall Street showing no real lead overnight, it's a good opportunity for investors to sit on their hands."
With local markets on tenterhooks ahead of a possible easing announcement, the addition of a rally in US bonds was all that was needed to give the local bank sector a fillip.

National Australia, up two cents to A$15.87 (US$12.11), Westpac gaining 18 cents to A$7.68 and Commonwealth Bank climbing 20 cents to A$12.95 all reached record highs before easing while ANZ Bank, up 12 cents to A$8.16 was also strong.
"The banking sector is looking pretty good," the dealer said, singling out Commonwealth Bank partly paid instalment receipts, which jumped over three percent, as noteworthy.
"Those recipts have put in a strong performance over the last few days."

Commonwealth Bank receipts closed 27 cents higher at A$8.77. Drug developer Biota also featured as investors raised their hopes for its anti-influenza treatment after favourable media coverage in the U.S. and locally before succumbing to profit taking in the afternoon session. Its shares closed nine cents higher at A$3.60.
Falls slightly shaded rises, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
